==English==

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|la|fascinātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|fascinō||to enchant, bewitch, fascinate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|fascinum||a phallus-shaped amulet worn around the neck in Ancient Rome; witchcraft}} + {{m|la|-ō|id=denominative|pos=verb-forming suffix}}, itself of obscure origin.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfæsɪneɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-fascinate.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[evoke]] an [[intense]] [[interest]] or [[attraction]] in someone.
#: {{ux|en|The flickering TV '''fascinated''' the cat.}}
# To make someone hold [[motionless]]; to [[spellbind]].
#: {{ux|en|We were '''fascinated''' by the potter's skill.}}
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=Leo, too, was strangely touched. Hitherto he had been '''fascinated''' against his better judgment, something as a bird is '''fascinated''' by a snake, but now I think that all this passed away, and he realised that he really loved this strange and glorious creature, as, alas! I loved her also.}}
# To be [[irresistibly]] [[charming]] or [[attractive]] to.
#: {{ux|en|Her gait '''fascinates''' all men.}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|fascinated|fascinating|fascinator|fascinoma|refascinate|unfascinating}}

====Related terms====
